Question ID: SPEECH_U04_L06_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.02

Source: Clear supporting details help listeners follow a speech. Which detail supports that central idea?

answer.text: A. Use a random detail from the source

feedback.text: This choice is too weak because it does not connect source structure, evidence, or central idea to the speech task.

answer.text: B. Choose a detail only because it is short

feedback.text: This choice may mention the topic, but it misses how the source supports clear communication for an audience.

answer.text: C. A speech that jumps between unrelated ideas can cause listeners to miss the purpose

feedback.text: Correct. This choice uses the source accurately and connects the source information to research-supported speech communication.

answer.text: D. Use evidence without explaining the connection

feedback.text: This choice does not give the speaker a reliable way to use source information in a speech.

Question ID: SPEECH_U04_L06_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best identifies central idea support?

answer.text: A. A detail supports the central idea when it explains or develops that main message

feedback.text: Correct. This choice uses the source accurately and connects the source information to research-supported speech communication.

answer.text: B. Choose a detail only because it is short

feedback.text: This choice may mention the topic, but it misses how the source supports clear communication for an audience.

answer.text: C. Ignore the source central idea

feedback.text: This choice reflects a misconception. Check the source purpose, central idea, and support before choosing evidence.

answer.text: D. Use evidence without explaining the connection

feedback.text: This choice does not give the speaker a reliable way to use source information in a speech.
